newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to hold Guiana talks after student riots.
newsitem.headline: France to hold Guiana talks after student riots.

text.p: The French government said on Tuesday that it would hold wide-ranging talks next year on the situation in French Guiana after student riots shook the South American territory last week.

France sent police reinforcements to the territory's capital Cayenne after one man died and seven, including six police, were injured in two days of rioting sparked by a strike of high school students demanding better conditions in schools.

Jean-Jacques de Peretti, Minister of Overseas Territories, said he would visit Guiana shortly with Education Minister Francois Bayrou, and would organise a conference there next year "because the future of the Guianese is a matter for the Guianese themselves".

De Peretti told the National Assembly that the problems of the territory, on the northeast coast of South America, stemmed largely from illegal immigration and a sharp increase in population to 140,000 from 80,000 over the past 13 years.
He said the students' demands for more teachers were legitimate and an increase in teaching jobs this year had been insufficient.

French Guiana is the only non-independent territory in South America. Its economy lags behind mainland France and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force. Joblessness is particularly acute among the young.
